body.heading: Where in the world is Nigeria?
paragraphs: Nigeria is a country in Western Africa, which is part of Africa.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Nigeria is Abuja.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Nigeria is English.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Nigeria is the Nigerian naira.

body.heading: How big is Nigeria?
paragraphs: Nigeria covers about 924,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of Sudan.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Yankari is Nigeria's best-known wildlife park, with elephants, lions and baboons — plus the Wikki Warm Spring, a natural pool that stays warm all year for a swim.
Olumo Rock is a giant granite outcrop that once sheltered the town of Abeokuta — 'under the rock'. Climb its stairs and lifts for views over a sea of rust-red rooftops.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Nigeria on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Nigeria in one breath: a country in Western Africa, capital Abuja, where people speak English and pay with the Nigerian naira.
materials: A globe, atlas or world map (to find Nigeria)
Paper and crayons or pencils for the screen-free mission
supervision: Read this one together: a grown-up can help with tricky place names and hunt for Nigeria on the map as you read.
safetyNotes: Reading only — no physical activity is involved.
If your family ever visits the watery places in this article, water fun in Nigeria always needs a grown-up watching closely.
